title: out-of-order-token-ingest-resequencer-and-fallback-allocator
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Edge proxies and regional ingress pipelines occasionally produce out-of-order or late-arriving token events for multi-route requests (bursts + retries). These cause incorrect per-tenant consumption totals, double-counting during real-time billing and noisy alerting when the ledger writes reject as duplicates. Existing mitigation (heuristic dedupe and wide windows) either (a) delays recognition for real-time dashboards or (b) misattributes credits during interleaved sessions.

Goal: Implement an ingestion-layer resequencer with lightweight provisional allocation semantics plus a deterministic fallback allocator that: (1) orders events within a tunable window using provenance hashing and watermarks, (2) writes idempotent provisional ledger entries tagged as PROVISIONAL, and (3) runs a bounded reconciliation job to convert provisional entries to final allocations or reclaim credits on late duplicates. The design should preserve sub-second reads for SLAs while guaranteeing eventual ledger convergence for billing.

Scope: prototype resequencer component (stateless shard with compact state synced to checkpoint store), modify token-writer to accept provisional writes, reconciliation worker to finalize or rollback provisional rows, migration strategy for historical late-arrival spikes, and observability + alarms.

Non-goals: full rework of billing pricing engine; after-the-fact invoice adjustments (this job will emit signals for finance but not automatically edit invoices).
comments: 2025-01-16 - Aisha: Drafted RFC and spike notes. Spike shows 99.95% of late events fall within a 22s window keyed by session id. Using provenance-hash (route+session+ingest-partition+offset) gives deterministic order for 98% of cases.
2025-01-22 - Marco: POC of resequencer using Kafka Streams + RocksDB local state. Memory looks reasonable but checkpoint write amplification observed under partition rebalance.

2025-01-27 - PM Rahul: Confirmed product acceptance criteria and emphasized minimal change to invoicing flow. Finance wants a runnable dry-run mode to surface delta reports before finalizing any credits.

2025-01-30 - Eng review: Decided to tag provisional entries with a monotonic tombstone and sequence id to support idempotent retries. Trade-off: requires tight retention of provisional window metadata for 48 hours.
2025-02-03 - Infra: Added requirement to support S3-backed cold checkpoints for long rebalances. Performance test scheduled week of 2025-02-10.
acceptance_criteria: Resequencer ingests simulated out-of-order stream in canary region and outputs ordered events with latency < 150ms median and 2s P95 within normal load
Token-writer accepts PROVISIONAL writes and exposes API to finalize/rollback by provenance-hash + sequence id
Reconciliation worker converts >99.9% of provisional entries to final within 10 minutes for typical load; false-positive rollbacks < 0.01%
End-to-end integration tests + dry-run reports show no net change in invoices for historical month under 24h of canary traffic
Alerting: a new metering dashboard with probes for provisional backlog, reconciliation lag, and duplicate-rate is published
tasks: RFC: finalize windowing model and provenance-hash algorithm (Aisha) - done
POC: resequencer Kafka Streams app + local RocksDB state (Marco) - in progress
Implement provisional write schema + migration script for token-ledger (DB PR)
Reconciliation worker: idempotent finalizer with bounded parallelism and cold storage checkpoints
Load test scenario: replays of synthetic late-arrival spikes + real historical buffer
Instrument dashboards and on-call runbook for provisional backlog
Dry-run: produce reconciliation delta reports for finance review (no invoice changes)
